source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A surgical mask alone even when blood or body fluid could splash into the nurse's eyes","B":"Eye or face protection with other indicated PPE when splash or spray exposure is anticipated","C":"Gloves alone because standard precautions do not require mucous-membrane protection from splashes","D":"Eye protection only when the client specifically requests additional protective equipment"}}
source_row.rationale: Standard precautions require eye protection (goggles or a face shield) whenever a procedure or activity carries a reasonably anticipated risk of blood or body fluid splash or spray to the face, protecting the mucous membranes of the eyes from potential pathogen exposure, in addition to other appropriate PPE such as gloves and a mask/gown as indicated.
source_row.source_detail: CDC Core Infection Prevention Practices: eye/face mucous-membrane protection for anticipated splashes or sprays; accessed 2026-08-14.
